title: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer Quits After a Really Rough Year
summary: Being the prime minister is a tough job, and for Keir Starmer, it just got too tough. On Monday, he announced he's quitting as leader of the Labour Party, which means he'll also stop being the UK's prime minister once his party picks a new leader. So what went wrong? For months, Starmer's poll numbers were really bad—meaning most people didn't think he was doing a good job. Then things got worse. He got a lot of criticism for picking Peter Mandelson as his ambassador to the U.S. last year. And in May, elections for local councils and the parliaments in Wales and Scotland were a disaster for Labour. Several top ministers quit, including the health secretary, Wes Streeting. Then, a simmering argument over defense spending boiled over, and the defense secretary, John Healey, resigned too. That was a huge blow. At the same time, Andy Burnham, the mayor of Greater Manchester, won a special election to become an MP. Burnham is very popular, and many Labour MPs wanted him to take over. Starmer tried to hold on, but over the weekend he realized he didn't have enough support. Now, Burnham is the only candidate to replace him. If no one else runs, he becomes leader automatically—and could be prime minister by mid-July. That's super fast! But it also means some big meetings Starmer planned, like a NATO summit and a UK-EU summit, are now up in the air. The UK is in for a quick and bumpy change at the top.
why_it_matters: When a country's top leader changes suddenly, important plans like helping Ukraine or making trade deals can be delayed, and those plans affect jobs and prices that families—even kids' schools—depend on.

background_read: In the United Kingdom, the prime minister is the head of the government, similar to a president in other countries. The prime minister is usually the leader of the political party that has the most MPs in Parliament.
The Labour Party is one of the two biggest parties in the UK. Keir Starmer became its leader and then prime minister in 2024 after his party won the general election. Before that, he was a lawyer.

A 'local council' is a group of people elected to run a town or small area—they make decisions about things like schools, parks, and roads. Elections for these councils can show how popular the national government is.
Article_Structure: WHO: Keir Starmer (outgoing prime minister), Andy Burnham (likely successor), key ministers like John Healey and Wes Streeting.
WHAT: Starmer announced he will quit as Labour leader and prime minister after losing support in his party.
WHERE: United Kingdom—the change affects the whole country and its relationships with allies.
WHY: Bad poll numbers, a controversial ambassador pick, disastrous local elections, and ministers resigning all piled up until Starmer no longer had enough backing to stay in charge.

perspectives.description: Many Labour MPs think Andy Burnham is more popular with the public and can win the next election. They believe a quick change gives the party a fresh start and might fix the government's problems.
Some people feel Starmer wasn't given enough time. They say the criticism made it impossible to lead, and that constant attacks from inside his own party were unfair.

Observers note that this fast turnover shows how unstable British politics has become. A leadership change right before big international meetings could make the UK look less reliable to other countries.
